text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000425's 99215 use runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity band and is concentrated in low-complexity patients, but too few charts came back to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern. The 99215 share is above the all-provider rate at nearly every condition count, including patients with no chronic conditions and patients with one. Most sampled 99215s are on 0–1 condition patients with acute or nonspecific diagnoses such as rash, URI, abdominal pain and follow-up (e.g., C0213439, C0213628, C0213702, C0214752). That is not explained by a sicker panel. Higher-complexity 99215s like C0213586 and C0214351 look plausible, and the gap in the 5+ band is small. The documentation is too thin to judge. Only 2 documented 99215s came back, both supported, and one (C0213894) is a one-condition hypertension patient documented at high MDM with no minutes recorded. The 2 of 20 unsupported 99214s (C0213629, C0214544) are above the comparison rate but rest on a very small count. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s and check whether the MDM and time support level 5 for those diagnoses, watching for templated or cloned notes."}
